newsitem.title: JAPAN: Matsushita Elec sees 97/98 DVD sales surge.
newsitem.headline: Matsushita Elec sees 97/98 DVD sales surge.

text.p: Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd said on Thursday it expects total shipments of digital videodisc players in the Japanese market to grow to 500,000 units in 1997/98, up from an estimated 150,000 units in the current year.

Matsushita also said it expects the electronics industry's total shipments, both domestically and for export, in the financial year starting on April 1 to rise four percent to a record 42.7 trillion yen.

Expected fast growth in sales of digital products such as digital video cameras, digital still cameras and minidisc players would lead the strong growth in 1997/98, Matsushita director Yoshio Hino told a news conference.
Matsushita expects exports by Japanese electronics makers for 1997/98 to rise by five percent to 15 trillion yen, partly aided by the weak yen and a recovery in semiconductor prices.
Matsushita used a yen rate of 110 yen to the dollar for its estimates for shipments in the next fiscal year, Hino said.

It expects domestic sales in the current year to rise six percent to 26.8 trillion yen, but to slow in 1997/98 to a rise of three percent, for a total of 27.7 trillion yen, affected by a continuing decline in product prices.

Hino also said that emerging new consumer products like DVDs, satellite television equipment such as set-top boxes and tuners, and digital TVs would start having a full impact on the market and electronics makers' earnings in the second half of calendar 1998.
"Because prices of set-top boxes are still high, we don't expect a large sales increase in digital broadcasting tuners in the next fiscal year," Hino said.
Matsushita expects Japan's total shipments of digital broadcasting tuners to rise to 700,000 units in 1997/98, up from an estimated 400,000 units this year.
